_about: Every reign from Saul to Zedekiah: 3 over the united kingdom, 20 in Judah (Athaliah included), 20 in Israel (Tibni included). Dates are Thiele's (The Mysterious Numbers of the Hebrew Kings), Merrill's for Saul, David and Solomon. `coStart` is where a co-regency or a rival reign began, before the king ruled alone from `start`. `verdict` is the book's own formula (did right / did evil); `mixed` is used where the text says both. `tg` is the Theographic 'Reign of' event, used for the Judah anchors and for nothing else. `personId` is the People pack's id.

kings.name: Saul
kings.summary: Israel's first king, chosen when the people asked for a king like the nations; rejected for disobeying God, he died on Mount Gilboa.

kings.name: David
kings.summary: The shepherd king: seven years over Judah at Hebron, then thirty-three over all Israel from Jerusalem. God promised him a throne forever.

kings.name: Solomon
kings.summary: Wise, rich, and the builder of the Temple; his many foreign wives turned his heart after other gods, and the kingdom split after him.

kings.name: Rehoboam
kings.summary: Solomon's son. His harsh answer at Shechem tore away the ten northern tribes; Shishak of Egypt plundered Jerusalem in his fifth year.

kings.name: Abijam (Abijah)
kings.summary: A short reign spent at war with Jeroboam, whom he defeated in the hill country of Ephraim.

kings.name: Asa
kings.summary: Removed the idols and even deposed his grandmother; late in life he leaned on Aram and on physicians rather than on the LORD.

kings.name: Jehoshaphat
kings.summary: Sent teachers of the Law through Judah and sang his way to victory, but allied his house with Ahab's by marriage.

kings.name: Jehoram
kings.summary: Married Ahab's daughter Athaliah, killed his brothers, and walked in the ways of the kings of Israel; Edom revolted.

kings.name: Ahaziah
kings.summary: Reigned one year and was killed by Jehu while visiting his wounded uncle Joram of Israel.

kings.name: Athaliah
kings.summary: Ahab's daughter seized the throne and killed the royal family; only the infant Joash was hidden away in the Temple.

kings.name: Joash
kings.summary: Crowned at seven by the priest Jehoiada and repaired the Temple; after Jehoiada died he had his son Zechariah stoned.

kings.name: Amaziah
kings.summary: Did right, but not with a whole heart: he beat Edom, brought home its gods, and was routed when he challenged Israel.

kings.name: Uzziah (Azariah)
kings.summary: Fifty-two years of strength and prosperity; he grew proud, burned incense in the Temple, and died a leper. Isaiah saw the Lord in the year he died.

kings.name: Jotham
kings.summary: Ruled for his leper father, then alone; he built the upper gate of the Temple and grew mighty because he ordered his ways before God.

kings.name: Ahaz
kings.summary: Refused Isaiah's sign of Immanuel and bought Assyria's help instead, copying an altar from Damascus for the Temple.

kings.name: Hezekiah
kings.summary: Cleansed the Temple, kept a great Passover, and trusted the LORD when Sennacherib's army surrounded Jerusalem.

kings.name: Manasseh
kings.summary: The longest and worst reign in Judah: altars to Baal in the Temple and innocent blood through Jerusalem. Taken to Babylon in chains, he humbled himself.

kings.name: Amon
kings.summary: Followed his father's idolatry without his father's repentance, and was murdered by his own servants after two years.

kings.name: Josiah
kings.summary: King at eight; the Book of the Law was found in his eighteenth year and he turned the whole land back to God. Killed at Megiddo by Pharaoh Neco.

kings.name: Jehoahaz (Shallum)
kings.summary: Reigned three months before Neco took him to Egypt, where he died.

kings.name: Jehoiakim
kings.summary: Egypt's puppet, then Babylon's; he cut up Jeremiah's scroll and burned it in the fire a column at a time.

kings.name: Jehoiachin (Jeconiah)
kings.summary: Surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar after three months and was taken to Babylon with Ezekiel and ten thousand others; released from prison thirty-seven years later.

kings.name: Zedekiah
kings.summary: Judah's last king rebelled against Babylon despite Jeremiah's warnings; he saw his sons killed before he was blinded and taken to Babylon.

kings.name: Jeroboam I
kings.summary: Led the ten tribes away from David's house and set up golden calves at Bethel and Dan so they would not go up to Jerusalem.

kings.name: Nadab
kings.summary: Jeroboam's son, killed by Baasha within two years; the whole house of Jeroboam was wiped out as Ahijah had said.

kings.name: Baasha
kings.summary: Took the throne by murder and fortified Ramah against Judah.

kings.name: Elah
kings.summary: Killed by his chariot commander Zimri while drunk at a steward's house.

kings.name: Zimri
kings.summary: Reigned seven days, then burned the palace over himself when Omri besieged Tirzah.

kings.name: Tibni
kings.summary: Half the people followed Tibni and half followed Omri; Omri's side prevailed and Tibni died.

kings.name: Omri
kings.summary: An army commander who founded a dynasty and built Samaria as Israel's capital; Assyria called Israel 'the house of Omri' for a century.

kings.name: Ahab
kings.summary: Married Jezebel and served Baal; Elijah's great opponent. He died in battle at Ramoth-gilead, as Micaiah foretold.

kings.name: Ahaziah
kings.summary: Fell through a lattice and sent to ask Baal-zebub whether he would recover; Elijah told him he would not.

kings.name: Joram (Jehoram)
kings.summary: Ahab's son, king through Elisha's great miracles and the siege of Samaria; Jehu shot him in Naboth's field.

kings.name: Jehu
kings.summary: Anointed by Elisha's servant to wipe out Ahab's house and Baal worship, which he did; but he kept Jeroboam's golden calves.

kings.name: Jehoahaz
kings.summary: Israel was ground down by Aram until he sought the LORD, who gave them a deliverer.

kings.name: Jehoash (Joash)
kings.summary: Wept over the dying Elisha and struck the ground only three times; he beat Aram three times, and broke down Jerusalem's wall.

kings.name: Jeroboam II
kings.summary: Restored Israel's borders as Jonah had foretold; the wealth and injustice of his reign are what Amos and Hosea preached against.

kings.name: Zechariah
kings.summary: The fourth generation of Jehu, as God had promised; murdered in public after six months.

kings.name: Shallum
kings.summary: Murdered Zechariah and reigned one month before Menahem murdered him.

kings.name: Menahem
kings.summary: Paid Tiglath-pileser (Pul) a thousand talents of silver to keep his throne.

kings.name: Pekahiah
kings.summary: Menahem's son, killed in his own citadel by his officer Pekah.

kings.name: Pekah
kings.summary: Allied with Rezin of Damascus against Ahaz; Tiglath-pileser took Galilee and carried its people to Assyria.

kings.name: Hoshea
kings.summary: Israel's last king stopped paying tribute and looked to Egypt; Shalmaneser besieged Samaria for three years and it fell.
